The src comment never got it. The IsTokenOnItsLine remark has it only in an ambiguous form ('is taken anywhere on its line, its middle included, as a token a load of that line would read there'). The same unconditional 'anywhere on its line' also appears in threat-model.md:460-461, lazy-reading.md:203 and the #171 comment.

findings.claim: The #171 comment says the search takes the word 'in uncompressed stream data'. It also says 'Its reach is narrow: it needs ... uncompressed text holding the word or such a header'. In fact any stream whose raw bytes hold the word is taken. That includes a /FlateDecode stream whose deflate data is a stored block, which is zlib level 0 or an encoder's fallback for data that does not compress: the text lies there verbatim. An embedded file or an object stream compressed that way gives the same freed object, false Error and rebuild. The src texts (IsTokenOnItsLine, the acceptance comment) say 'stream data' without that qualifier, so they are right.

findings.fix: This is a design choice for the maintainer, since it qualifies round 2's [1] and the round 3 wording. Recommended fix: when the stream the table's /XRefStm read gives a /Prev, do not pass it over for a not-reached cross-reference stream candidate that gives none.
